classification.difficultyReason: Express deviations algebraically and connect their sum to the defining identity that the total equals the number of values times the mean. Generalising to an arbitrary data set requires symbolic reasoning, scaffolded by the three-value proof in part a.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Prove that the sum of the deviations for the data set $a,b,c$ is zero.

answer.short:
$(a-\bar{x})+(b-\bar{x})+(c-\bar{x})=0$.

Substitute $\bar{x}=\dfrac{a+b+c}{3}$ into the sum of the deviations.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Prove that the sum of the deviations of any data set is zero.

answer.short:
$(x_1-\bar{x})+\cdots+(x_n-\bar{x})=0$.

The sum of the data values equals $n\bar{x}$, so subtracting the mean from each of the $n$ values gives a total of zero.
answer.worked:
Let the data values be $x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_n$. Their mean is $\bar{x}=\dfrac{x_1+x_2+\cdots+x_n}{n}$. Therefore,
$$\begin{aligned}(x_1-\bar{x})+\cdots+(x_n-\bar{x})&=(x_1+\cdots+x_n)-n\bar{x}\\(x_1-\bar{x})+\cdots+(x_n-\bar{x})&=(x_1+\cdots+x_n)-n\left(\frac{x_1+\cdots+x_n}{n}\right)\\(x_1-\bar{x})+\cdots+(x_n-\bar{x})&=0.\end{aligned}$$
